title: Platner leads Collins in first UNH poll since Mills's exit - AOL.com
content: Oyster farmer Graham Platner, a Democrat, leads incumbent Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, in the Maine Senate race, a new poll from the University of New Hampshire Survey Center. The Pine Tree State poll, released May 27, is the first from the center since Platner’s main primary opponent, Gov. Janet Mills, withdrew from the race. Without Mills, Platner is now the clear favorite to win the Democratic primary with the support of 76% of likely Democratic voters. And in a hypothetical general election matchup against Collins, the poll found that 51% of general election voters say they would vote for Platner, while 42% would vote for Collins and 6% are undecided. The difference is largely unchanged since February, when Platner was leading 49% to 38%. Some of the top reasons likely Democratic primary voters said they supported Platner was his understanding or empathy (21%), his chance of winning the general election (18%), his policies (11%) and because they think he represents change (11%). The Maine Senate race is one of the most competitive and closely watched battles in the country as Democrats seek to flip control of the narrowly Republican-controlled Senate. But it’s still early: polls found Democrat Sara Gideon ahead of Collins in the 2020 race, too, but Collins ended up defeating her by nearly nine points. The poll surveyed 1,397 Maine residents online between May 21 – 25. It has a margin of error of +/-2.6%. Mills is term limited, so the race for Maine governor is open this year. The poll found that the Democratic primary for Maine governor is tied: 28% respectively of likely Democratic primary voters said they would vote for Maine Senate President Troy Jackson and former Director of the Maine Center for Disease Control Nirav Shah. Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows trails at 13%, as do former Speaker of  the Maine House of Representatives Hannah Pingree (12%) and energy executive Angus King III (7%). On the Republican side, however, former Assistant U.S. Secretary of state Robert Charles leads the field with 37%, up 9% from February. 18% say they would vote for health care executive Jonathan Bush, and several other candidates fall behind. Maine’s Second Congressional District, rated likely R by the Cook Political Report, also features an open seat after Rep. Jared Golden, D-Maine, decided against running for re-election. Former Gov. Paul LePage is running unchallenged on the Republican side. On the Democratic side, 23% of likely voters say their first choice would be former Congressional aide Jordan Wood, 22% support state Sen. Joe Baldacci, 17% are for Maine State Auditor Matthew Dunlap and 14% would vote for social worker Paige Loud. 25% are undecided. In the First Congressional District, two Republican candidates are looking to challenge Rep. Chellie Pingree, D-Maine. The poll found that 24% of likely Republican voters in this district would vote for 2024 nominee Ronald Russell, while 7% would vote for sales consultant Joshua Pietrowicz. 68% are undecided. Maine uses a ranked-choice voting system for both governor and federal primary races. Managed care companies are often judged by how well they balance member growth, medical spending, reimbursement conditions, and pricing discipline. The company is not simply an insurer; it also has a broad services platform that touches pharmacy benefits, clinical programs, and care delivery operations. That wider structure gives UnitedHealth several ways to manage health system costs, but it also places the company under close review whenever medical utilization trends shift. The decision is important because colorectal cancer screening has long faced participation challenges, partly due to the inconvenience and discomfort associated with traditional procedures. A blood-based option may help improve access by giving eligible members a simpler path to routine screening through a standard care setting. For insurers, preventive care can also support long-term cost management by encouraging earlier detection and reducing the risk of more complex treatment needs later. Stronger language around cost control, stable membership, and disciplined pricing could help support the current tone. However, continued pressure in medical utilization would keep scrutiny high. The company’s diversified business model may help soften some challenges, but it does not remove exposure to broader healthcare cost trends. That is why the earnings update matters for both UnitedHealth and the wider managed care group. UnitedHealth Group (NYSE:UNH), is heading into its earnings update with a stronger tone than it had during its recent difficult stretch. The rebound has brought attention back to cost control, health services performance, and the company’s ability to manage changing utilization trends. The colorectal screening coverage decision adds another layer by connecting the company to preventive care innovation. For a managed care leader, decisions like this can shape access, provider behaviour, and long-term cost strategy. The next update will decide whether the recent improvement reflects stronger fundamentals or only a short-term reset in sentiment. For now, UnitedHealth remains a major name to watch within managed care as earnings, coverage policy, and healthcare cost trends come together. title: UNH Poll: Markey’s Lead Over Moulton Narrows Ahead of September Democratic Primary - Swampscott Tides
content: A new University of New Hampshire poll suggests incumbent Sen. Ed Markey’s lead over Rep. Seth Moulton has narrowed ahead of September’s Democratic primary. Markey and Moulton are competing in the Democratic primary for Massachusetts’ U.S. Senate seat ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.  Moulton has called for a “new generation of leaders who listen more to the people that we represent and honestly represent their needs and concerns,” while Markey has said his bid is “about the people” and “powered by grassroots supporters from every corner of our Commonwealth.” The University of New Hampshire survey was conducted June 18-23 among 623 likely general election voters. “Markey and Moulton are both favored in general election matchups with presumptive Republican Senate nominee John Deaton,” the Bay State Poll read. “Incumbent Sen Ed Markey continues to lead Rep. Seth Moulton in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Massachusetts, but his lead has narrowed.” Among likely Democratic primary voters, 41% said they support Markey, while 35% back Moulton. An additional 24% are still undecided, and 1% would vote for another candidate. “The momentum on the ground is undeniable, and this poll proves what we’ve been hearing in every single town: Massachusetts voters are completely sick of the same old, tired Washington politics,” said Taylor Hebble, campaign spokesperson for Moulton’s campaign. Markey’s support has fallen from 46% in April. Undecided voters have increased in the last two months as well, rising from 15%. Moulton leads among moderates, with 70% support, while slim majorities of liberals (51%) and progressives (52%) back Markey. Markey also holds a 67% advantage among self-identified socialists. Markey’s overall net favorability rating (the percentage of those who have a favorable rating minus those who are unfavorable) among Democratic primary voters fell to +30 from +42 in April. Moulton’s net favorability also declined, dropping from +24 in April to +11. Polling from May similarly found Markey holding a five-point lead over Moulton. The Emerson College Polling found Markey leading 37% to 32%, with 29% of voters undecided. An April 15 poll by the Suffolk University Political Research Center and the Boston Globe showed 79-year-old incumbent Markey at 47%, while 47-year-old Iraq War veteran Moulton had edged up to 30.4%. The primary is September 1, with early voting starting August 22. title: UNH hockey recruit Parker Von Richter picked by Pittsburgh in NHL Draft - AOL.com
content: BUFFALO —University of New Hampshire men's hockey recruit Parker Von Richter of Mississauga, Ontario was selected by the Pittsburgh Penguins June 27 in the 2026 NHL Draft at the KeyBank Center. Von Richter was drafted in the fourth round with the 111th overall pick. Von Richter has played in the OHL for four seasons totaling 25 goals and 94 assists for 119 points. Von Richter played for the Barrie Colts during the 2025-26 season as the defenseman posted eight goals and 16 assists for 24 points. He also totaled two goals and 12 assists for 14 points during the playoffs as the team reached the OHL Championship Series. At the start of the 2025-26 season, Von Richter was an alternate captain for the Brampton Steelheads appearing in 38 games with four goals and 21 assists for 25 points. He also recorded eight goals and 22 assists for 30 points for Brampton in 2024-25. Von Richter was a two-year member of the Mississauga Steelheads, tallying five goals and 35 assists for 40 points over the two seasons. UNH has now had 102 players selected in the NHL Draft in program history. The Wildcats start the 2026-27 season at Quinnipiac Oct. 2 and begin the home season versus Michigan State Oct. 23-24. UnitedHealth Group delivered 41.5% returns over the last year. See how this stacks up to the rest of the Healthcare industry. The P/E ratio is usually a useful way to compare how the market is pricing UnitedHealth Group against other healthcare stocks, using its earnings as a common yardstick. UnitedHealth Group currently trades at about 32.1x earnings, which is higher than the broader Healthcare industry average of around 25.9x. However, it sits below both the peer group average of 39.4x and a modelled fair P/E of about 42.6x that reflects the company’s size, profitability profile and risk factors. The gap between the current 32.1x and the 42.6x fair ratio indicates that the market is applying a discount relative to what this framework suggests could be reasonable for UnitedHealth Group. Recent analyst optimism around upcoming earnings has supported sentiment in the stock. In that context, the fact that the P/E still sits below this tailored fair ratio can be viewed as a potential valuation cushion rather than a sign of excessive enthusiasm.
